Hi Anita / Ravi —

Great to meet you this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a few next steps so we can build a tailored cost model for the workflow you described.

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Primary use case: real-time risk scoring and enrichment for transaction flows during market hours. Low tolerance for tail latency.
- Data residency: US-only.
- Target go-live: Q3 2026; pilot in next 30–60 days.
- Key question: whether Hosted API can meet SLOs/cost targets, or if Dedicated (reserved capacity) / Private (VPC or on-prem) is needed for predictable latency and data controls.

What I need from you to run accurate cost modeling:
1) Expected monthly token volume (prompt+response) or example daily volumes
2) Typical token length per request (average prompt + completion)
3) Peak concurrent requests or RPS during market hours
4) Latency SLO (p50/p95 target) and any absolute max latency threshold
5) Any compliance docs you need (SOC 2, ISO, attestations) for Private deployment planning

Attached is our quick reference on Dedicated tiers (redwood_dedicated_tiers.pdf). If you can send the bullets above, I’ll run a Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private cost comparison and share a short spreadsheet with estimates + recommended next steps.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You send usage numbers (this week)
- I’ll return a cost model and recommendation (2 business days after numbers)
- Optional: 30-day pilot or POC on Dedicated if you want full throughput validation

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-minute follow-up if that helps.

Best,

Thanks Anita — this is great detail and exactly what we need. I put together a short, conservative cost model and attached the spreadsheet (pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx). High-level summary below.

Quick answers to your questions:
- Dedicated tiers: we size reserved commits around sustained throughput targets and provide guidance in tokens/sec and nominal concurrent requests. Typical mapping (example):
  - Small commit (~2,000 tokens/sec sustained): supports ~15–25 concurrent real-time requests at ~200–300 tokens/request with low p95 latency
  - Medium (~8,000 tokens/sec): supports ~60–100 concurrent requests at similar request sizes
  - Large (>20,000 tokens/sec): for very high concurrency or low tail-latency at scale
- Hosted per-token assumptions: we model effective per-token cost using observed batching, KV/prefix cache hits, and expected concurrency. For real-time scoring we assume limited batching (conservative) and include small overhead for network + routing.

High-level cost comparison (monthly, rough order of magnitude for your numbers: 350M tokens/month, peak concurrency 120):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): ~ $0.0009 per token effective (conservative) => ~ $315,000/month. Pros: fastest to production, minimal ops. Cons: cost at scale and tail-latency less predictable for peak bursts unless we add higher-priority SLA.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): example medium tier commit: ~$55,000/month for the reserved pool sized to support your sustained peak (~8k tokens/sec); plus a small overage per token. For your profile, expected total effective cost around $120k–$160k/month depending on commit and utilization. Pros: predictable unit economics, lower per-token cost, better tail-latency. Cons: minimum monthly commitment; requires planning for burst windows.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time onboarding + license (example: $250k–$500k upfront) + infra (customer-managed GPU fleet) + annual support. For sustained, heavy usage and strict KMS/data residency, Private can be cost-effective long-term but requires ops investment.

Caveats & assumptions:
- Hosted estimate uses conservative batching (minimal) and no prefix caching benefits. If you can tolerate slightly higher latency windows to enable batching or reuse cached prefixes for repeated prompts, hosted costs drop substantially (~20–40%).
- Dedicated estimate assumes an 80% utilization on committed GPUs; lower utilization increases effective cost per token.
- Private estimate excludes customer infra procurement and network costs.

Attachments: pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx (line-item estimate + sensitivity by utilization) and redwood_dedicated_tiers.pdf (detailed tier mapping).

Recommended next steps:
1) We can provision a short Dedicated pilot (30 days) sized to your peak window so you can validate p95/p99 under load. We’ll provide a temporary discount for pilot commits.
2) If you prefer Hosted to start, we can enable a higher-priority SLA route during market hours and revisit commits after 30 days of production traffic.
3) If compliance or KMS is a blocker, we’ll scope Private deployment pricing and SOW.

If this looks good I can produce a formal SOW and line-item pricing (includes committed tier, pilot discount, onboarding, and optional support). Would you and Ravi be available for a 30-minute pricing review Thursday or next Monday?

Best,
